accepted.reason: Good observation-target alignment given surveillance semantics: hospital admissions plausibly lag an infectious proxy, and delayed_I avoids introducing a potentially weakly identifiable H compartment in a short (31-week) single-season series. Complexity is moderate and consistent with prior discovery patterns.

Same strengths as proposal 0 with an alternative plausible fixed lag; keeping structure identical while varying delay is a reasonable pre-fit sensitivity check. Still avoids H identifiability issues and matches recommended delayed_I mapping.

Parsimonious alternative that retains the key delayed_I observation mechanism while reducing state/parameter complexity vs SEIRS. Appropriate to include as a simpler comparator when waning immunity is not strongly supported by a single-season window.

rejected.reason: Although H aligns semantically with hospitalization rate, adding an explicit H compartment (SEIHR) increases complexity and raises identifiability risk in a short single-season series; surveillance note explicitly flags H as potentially weakly identifiable here. Also, mapping weekly admissions to an H stock-like compartment can be a mismatch unless H is clearly defined as incident admissions.

I+H observation map risks semantic mismatch for a hospitalization-rate target (admissions) and can blur distinct processes (infection prevalence vs hospitalization burden). It also inherits H identifiability concerns from SEIHR and may over-flexibly fit level/width without clear justification in this short series.

suggested_edits.edit: Clarify the intended meaning of H (incident admissions vs hospitalized census). If H is a stock, consider adding an observation delay or redefining the observation mapping to better represent weekly admissions; otherwise this template risks observation-target misalignment and weak identifiability in 31 weeks.

Provide a stronger semantic justification for why admissions would be proportional to I+H (e.g., reporting behaves like a blended burden proxy). If the target is strictly incident admissions, prefer delayed_I (or H if well-defined as incidence) to avoid conflating prevalence and hospitalization states.
